title: feat(hooks): onTool regex filter per rule, checked before the dispatcher boots (stacked on #764)
description:
## .what

let a role register a hook rule with a declared **`onTool` filter** — a regex over the tool name and over the tool input — that rhachet evaluates **before it boots**. a call no rule wants then exits in a few ms, with zero bun / rhachet boot.

🔗 **stacked on #764** (one dispatcher process per event). build after it lands: the filter lives in front of that one dispatcher.

## .why — measured, one Bash tool call (`pwd`), 10 hooks

| shape | cpu per Bash call | peak rss |
|---|---|---|
| today: 10 separate hook processes | ~2010–2110 ms | 207 MB |
| after #764: one in-process dispatcher | ~1200 ms est. | 52 MB |
| **after #764 + this: a call no rule wants** | **a few ms (one `sh` + one `grep`)** | ~0 |

- the 3 rhx hooks alone are ~1350 ms (67%) of today's cost, and on a plain `pwd` none of them applies
  - `route.mutate.guard`, `route.foreground.guard`, `route.bounce`: matter only when a route is bound to the branch; on an unbound branch every call is a miss
  - `memory.guard`: matters only when the call names a claude memory path
  - `route.mutate.guard` also fires on **Read**, which cannot mutate
- a typical busy session's calls are mostly misses for every rule, so most calls would drop from ~1200 ms to a few ms

## .shape

- a rule declares, for example:
  ```ts
  onTool: {
    name: /^(Write|Edit|Bash)$/,
    input: /\/memory\/|MEMORY\.md/,
    when: { fileExists: '<the path route.bind.set writes>' },  // optional precondition
  }
  ```
- `rhx init --hooks` compiles every rule's filter for an event into the ONE registered command as a posix pre-check, e.g. `sh -c 'grep -qE "<union of input regexes>" || [ -e <bind file> ] || exit 0; exec rhx hooks.dispatch --event PreToolUse'`
- the claude `matcher` field becomes the union of the rules' `name` regexes, so claude itself skips the event for a tool no rule names
- inside the dispatcher, each rule runs only if its own filter matches
- a rule with no `onTool` keeps today's behavior (always runs)

## .done bar

- on an unbound branch, a Bash `pwd` call costs ≤ ~10 ms cpu in hooks and zero rhx boots, per `rhx claude.hooks.cost --tool Bash` (uladkasach/dev-env-setup)
- bhrain's `route.*` guards and `memory.guard` declare their filters; `route.mutate.guard` drops `Read`, or states what a read is guarded against
